prompt:
Write 9 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim, in time order. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1445; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- The patient was treated for the same body area within the last two years, and that condition adds to the current complaints.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim received for a sideswipe that occurred while the insured's vehicle was changing lanes. The claimant is represented by counsel, and all further contact will be routed through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Reviewed the police report, which places the claimant inside the vehicle at the time of impact. Statements from the other driver and two independent witnesses describe the collision the same way the claimant did.

Entry 3: Photographs of the scene and both vehicles were uploaded to the file. The damage pattern is largely consistent with the impact described, with most of it concentrated along the passenger-side panels.

Entry 4: Confirmed with the policy records that the driver involved is listed as a named driver on the policy. Coverage was in force at the time of loss, and nothing in the vehicle history points to damage that predates the policy start.

Entry 5: Spoke with the claimant's attorney, who reported whiplash symptoms. The claimant has given the same account of events in every conversation so far, without material variation.

Entry 6: Medical records show the claimant was treated for the same body area within the past two years. The earlier condition appears to add to the current complaints, and the treating provider has been asked to separate the two in the notes.

Entry 7: The reported injury is consistent with the type and force of the collision. Treatment has followed a typical course, with visits tapering as the claimant's symptoms improved.

Entry 8: No prior damage to the insured vehicle is known from inspection or from any previous claim on file. The repair estimate has been reviewed against the photos and the described impact.

Entry 9: File is being prepared for the next review step. Remaining items include the final treatment summary from the provider and the attorney's demand letter, once received.
